info.description:
This is the HTTP trading API for Smarkets. It can be used to trade on our exchange.

For authenticated requests:
  • Get a session token using the login route: GET /v3/sessions/
  • Click on 'Authorize 🔓', enter your token after 'Session-Token ' and click on the 'Authorize' button

In order to place bets and get the latest prices without restrictions using this API, you need to be a Smarkets API user.

Rate limits

All API users are subject to a default rate limit of 1200 requests per 60 seconds across all endpoints, applied per account. Individual endpoints may have additional stricter limits as documented on each route below.

When rate limited, the API returns a 429 response with error type RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Rate limit status is also returned in the following response headers:

  • X-RateLimit-Limit - Maximum requests allowed in the current window
  • X-RateLimit-Remaining - Requests remaining in the current window
  • X-RateLimit-Reset - Seconds until the rate limit window resets

The outcome of the contract can be:
  • winner: This contract is the winner or one of the winners of the market
  • loser: This contract is a loser
  • deadheat: There was a tie between this contract and another one. This is quite a rare outcome.
  • reduce: This contract was withdrawn from the market and a reduction factor was applied.
  • void: This contract is no longer allowed to be traded on.

quantity.description:
Quantity is the sum of the total pot (back+lay) in case the order is matched
The units are 1/100 of a UK penny.
Example: Quantity 500 = 0.05 GBP
To convert it to back stake, just multiply by the price and divide by 100000000
Example: 100000 (quantity) * 5000 (price) / 100000000 = 5 GBP back stake
The minimum stake is £0.05 or currency equivalent

quantity_filled.description: The quantity in GBP of the order that was matched

quantity_filled_pending.description:
The quantity in GBP of the order that was matched and pending confirmation.
Bets will be subject to an eight second ‘Pending’ confirmation delay after being matched.
If no significant events occur in this period, the bet is confirmed.
If our scouting feed tells us that a material event (a goal, red card, or penalty) or a set-piece event (corner or dangerous free-kick) might have occurred, the Pending period is extended until we get confirmation either way.
If subsequent messages confirm that a material event has occurred, we void those bets matched in the preceding eight seconds.
This is to protect users from courtsiding and faster feeds.

type.description:
Order types can have the following values:
  • good_til_cancelled: this order will be open until a reduction factor is applied or a market state changes to live, which will cancel the order.
  • keep_in_play: the same as good_til_cancelled, except it will not be cancelled on market state changes
  • good_til_halted: the same as good_til_cancelled, except a market
  • immediate_or_cancel: if the minimum_accepted_quantity is not matched at the time of order placement, this order will be cancelled.
  • over_the_counter: this order was matched right after being created.

The following table explains the lifetime of orders:

order_type Market Goes Live Market Halted Reduction Factor Applied
good_til_cancelled Cancelled Cancelled Cancelled
good_til_halted Kept Cancelled Cancelled
keep_in_play Kept Kept Cancelled

Orders marked as immediate_or_cancel must be executed immediately and thus will not remain in the book.

Same happens to orders marked as over_the_counter which are executed immediately.

contract_selections.description:
These particular contracts are not related to markets in the same way that most contracts are related to markets.
The contract_selections field is only set for accumulator markets and it refers to the contract IDs that the acca is made up of, an example:

M1 (Winner market in Man Utd - Liverpool)
  • M1-C1 (Man Utd)
  • M1-C2 (Draw)
  • M1-C3 (Liverpool)
M2 (Winner market in Arsenal - Chelsea)
  • M2-C1 (Arsenal)
  • M2-C2 (Draw)
  • M2-C3 (Chelsea)

Now an accumulator market is created:
M3 (Man Utd and Arsenal both to win on 23rd of February)
  • M3-C1 (Yes)
  • M3-C2 (No)

In this case, M3 will have two contracts (M3-C1 and M3-C2) but contract_selections will be M1-C1 (Man Utd) and M2-C1 (Arsenal).

get.description:
## Description Events in Smarkets follow a tree structure per sport, where events can have several child events, but only one parent event.
As an example for football, we have:
  • The root event which is the sport - Football
  • Child events which are leagues - Premier League, La Liga, etc
  • Grandchild events which are football matches - Man U vs Chelsea, ...

In the case of most sports, we have 3 levels in the tree. However, there are cases where we can have a different number.

To identify whether an event is a leaf node in this tree, one can look at the bettable flag.

Only leaf events can have markets, which in turn will have contracts.

M1 (Winner market in Man Utd - Liverpool)
  • M1-C1 (Man Utd)
  • M1-C2 (Draw)

If subsequent messages confirm that a material event has occurred, we void those bets matched in the preceding eight seconds.
This is to protect users from courtsiding and faster feeds.

Order types can have the following values:
  • good_til_cancelled: this order will be open until a reduction factor is applied or a market state changes to live, which will cancel the order.
  • keep_in_play: the same as good_til_cancelled, except it will not be cancelled on market state changes
  • good_til_halted: the same as good_til_cancelled, except a market
  • immediate_or_cancel: if the minimum_accepted_quantity is not matched at the time of order placement, this order will be cancelled.
  • over_the_counter: this order was matched right after being created.

The following table explains the lifetime of orders:

order_type Market Goes Live Market Halted Reduction Factor Applied
good_til_cancelled Cancelled Cancelled Cancelled
good_til_halted Kept Cancelled Cancelled
keep_in_play Kept Kept Cancelled

Orders marked as immediate_or_cancel must be executed immediately and thus will not remain in the book.

Same happens to orders marked as over_the_counter which are executed immediately.

get.description:
## Description Events in Smarkets follow a tree structure per sport, where events can have several child events, but only one parent event.
As an example for football, we have:
  • The root event which is the sport - Football
  • Child events which are leagues - Premier League, La Liga, etc
  • Grandchild events which are football matches - Man U vs Chelsea, ...

In the case of most sports, we have 3 levels in the tree. However, there are cases where we can have a different number.

To identify whether an event is a leaf node in this tree, one can look at the bettable flag.

Only leaf events can have markets, which in turn will have contracts.

get.description:
## Description Retrieve all bettable children events and their parents (a subtree) starting from the event defined by the `event_id`. This route works by doing a BFS over the events tree - it will fetch all the children of the starting event, in the next iteration it will fetch the children of the children events and so on until there are no new events being found. At every level `ended_limit` ended events will be added as well. If at any point the `bettable_limit` of bettable events is reached the search will stop. If the starting event is bettable and has no children then only that event will be retrieved.

Additionally, this route offers the same functionality as the `/events/` route. Check description for `/events/` route for more details.

Name of the market. This field is for display purposes and should not be used to identify the market.
The market_type field should be used instead.

slug.description:
Slug concisely represents the market.
It should not be used to identify the market.
The market_type field should be used instead.

state.description:
Market state can have the following values:
-new: just created, still not open for trading
-open: open for trading not live in-play
-live: open for trading, live in-play
-halted: trading is halted temporarily, usually due to material events
-settled: traded has ceased and the market has settled
-voided: the market was voided and no winner was chosen
-unavailable: the maret is not available for betting

winner_count.description:
How many winners will the market have.
Usually this number is 1, except for "To Place", "Top x Finish" type markets

modified.description: The datetime of the last modification made by Smarkets to the event properties

name.description: The name of the event

parent_id.description: This ID uniquely identifies the parent of the event

seo_description.description: Additional description for this event used for SEO

short_name.description: A shorter version of the name of the event

slug.description: An easier way to identify the event

special_rules.description: Special rules to be defined for this market

start_date.description:
In what day the event will go live,
This can be useful for events that still have an unknown start_datetime

start_datetime.description: When the event is scheduled to go live

state.description:
Event state can have the following values:
  • upcoming: the event is now open for betting
  • live: the event is now live in-play
  • ended: the event has ended and its markets should be settled
  • settled: the event has ended and its markets should be settled
  • cancelled: the event was cancelled and didn't take place
  • suspended: the event was suspended and during play time

super_sub_enabled.description: True for events that are in super-sub leagues

type.description: The type of the event, for instance, the name of the sport

domain.description: The domain part of the type (football, politics, horse_racing, etc)

scope.description: The scope part of the event type (single_event, outright, acca, etc)

venue.description: Additional information about the state of this event

event_id.description: This ID uniquely identifies an event
